parts.text: SUPERVISOR DESIGN RULING — this answers EVAL_FEEDBACK finding 1's request for an explicit scope/design change, and supersedes the original acceptance design. (a) The manifest/--agent/init.tools contract is FORMALLY DROPPED: your round-1 evidence proved agy 1.1.15 does not enforce the allowlist, so the PreToolUse hook IS the accepted prevention design. Do not implement --agent or init.tools. Record this ruling in WORK_SUMMARY.md and the worklog. (b) NEW INTELLIGENCE resolving finding 2: per agy tool documentation, IsArtifact:true on write_to_file is meant ONLY for internal session-tracking documents (task checklists, ArtifactType "task") that live in the brain directory; the bug is the model MISAPPLYING IsArtifact:true to workspace deliverable files. Supervisor ran live unhooked tests today (agy 1.1.15, gemini-3.5-flash-low, temp workspaces): explicit "IsArtifact false" prompt → status SUCCESS once but the artifact-path ERROR in two later identical runs (prompting the flag is unreliable); trivial default write → SUCCESS; deliverable-style "write your proposal to proposal.md" → ERROR with the exact original error text; the workspace file was physically written in every case. CONCLUSION: plain native workspace writes are legal; only artifact-flagged out-of-brain writes crash. Therefore rewrite the hook policy: DENY only when the call carries artifact semantics (IsArtifact true, or ArtifactMetadata present — confirm exact arg names against the real payload schema you captured in round 2) AND the target is outside artifactDirectoryPath; the deny reason should instruct retrying the SAME write_to_file immediately with IsArtifact false (do not push the model to the shell). ALLOW all non-artifact writes anywhere and artifact writes inside the brain dir. Update the worklog with this refined mechanism (IsArtifact semantics, ArtifactType task, model-misapplication root cause). (c) Finding 3 scope change AUTHORIZED: you may now modify the ae5edb6 repair-retry — on artifact-path or hook-denial errors, retry in a FRESH conversation carrying the original prompt plus a corrective instruction (append "set IsArtifact to false on write_to_file calls"), instead of resuming the poisoned conversation; keep it bounded to one retry; update its tests. If feasible, add one bounded real Adapter.RunTurn proof of a denied-then-recovered turn. (d) Findings 4 and 5: fix exactly as written (preserve existing hooks.json file mode, document the advisory-lock boundary honestly, include both complete init.tools dumps in WORK_SUMMARY.md).

SUPERVISOR ADDENDUM (optional — must NOT jeopardize completing the required round-3 work, and its absence is NOT a defect): the user suggests a harness-level prompt layer as additional prevention. If cheap to do safely this round, prepend a short fixed preamble to the prompt in RunTurn (agy adapter only) along the lines of: "When creating or editing files in the workspace with write_to_file or related tools, never set IsArtifact to true and never attach ArtifactMetadata; those are only for agy's internal session-tracking documents in its private brain directory." Rationale: supervisor's live tests show prompting alone is unreliable (1 of 3), so this cannot replace the hook, but every hook denial burns a full turn + fresh-conversation retry, so reducing denial frequency is worth one static line. If you implement it: keep it a single constant, make sure it does not interfere with structured-output schemas or steering prompts, add a simple test that the preamble is present in the -p argument, and mention it in WORK_SUMMARY.md and the worklog as layer zero (prompt) ahead of layer one (hook) and layer two (repair-retry). If you skip it for time/risk, record it in the worklog as a designed-but-deferred layer with this rationale. Either choice is acceptable.
